# SPE Round r01 Plan: Ticket Triage Agent

Round r01 is the first round. There is no earlier evidence, so every prediction comes from my judgment. Many details are missing from the spec. I chose a default for each one and logged it in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. You can overrule any default before approving.

## 1. Specify

### Transcript
I will save your prompt word for word to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`. I will not edit that file.

### Requirements (`spe/spec/spec.md`, round r01 table)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns each ticket one category from a fixed list. | User: "triage tickets correctly". Default D1. | Category accuracy is at least 0.90 on the 60-ticket set. |
| R2 | The agent assigns each ticket a priority from P1 to P4. | User: "correctly". Default D2. | Priority exact match is at least 0.75. P1 recall is at least 0.95. |
| R3 | The agent returns valid JSON that matches `triage/schema.json`. | Decision: code needs to read the output. | Schema validity is 1.00. |
| R4 | The agent is cheap to run. | User: "cheaply". Default D4. | Mean cost per ticket is at most $0.006. The recommended config is the cheapest one that passes R1 to R3. |
| R5 | The agent sees only the ticket text. | Decision: a fair test. | The transcript scan finds no reads of gold labels, graders, or predictions. |

### Defaults and open decisions (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Default I chose | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Category list | `bug`, `feature_request`, `billing`, `account_access`, `how_to`, `spam` | User |
| D2 | Priority rubric | P1 is an outage, data loss, or a security issue. P2 is broken for a customer with no workaround. P3 has a workaround. P4 is cosmetic or a question. | User |
| D3 | Ticket data | No real tickets exist. I will write 60 synthetic tickets. I pick each label first and then write the ticket to match it. That gives 10 tickets per category and 12 P1 tickets. | User. Real tickets would make r02 stronger. |
| D4 | Cost target | $0.006 per ticket at list prices | User |
| D5 | Models | Opus is `claude-opus-5-5`. I will confirm the Sonnet model ID in the claude-api reference before I write the harness. | Logged default |
| D6 | Who writes the gold labels | I write them. I flag ambiguous tickets in the file. I recommend that you spot-check 12 tickets. The round goes ahead without your check. | User |
| D7 | Stack | Python 3.12 and the `anthropic` SDK. The agent returns output through one tool call with a JSON schema. Temperature stays at the default. | Logged default |
| D8 | Control regrade | r01 has no earlier round to regrade. I will grade one recorded answer file twice instead. Both runs must give the same score. | Logged default |
| D9 | Few-shot examples | I write 8 examples separately from the eval set. A script checks that no example overlaps an eval ticket. | Logged default |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations
Each config changes exactly one thing from the config before it.

| Config | Model | Prompt | Change from previous |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | Opus | Category list and priority names only | Baseline |
| C1 | Opus | C0 plus the D2 rubric and 8 few-shot examples | Adds the label guide |
| C2 | Sonnet | Same prompt as C1 | Swaps the model |

### Numbers
A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. The naive guess for r01 is that all three configs score the same as C0. The `same_as_last_round` field is null because r01 has no earlier round.

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | 0.82 ± 0.06 | 0.90 ± 0.05 | 0.87 ± 0.06 | `grade.py::category_exact` | The guide settles the boundary cases, such as billing versus account access. Sonnet loses a few of the ambiguous tickets. |
| Priority exact match | 0.62 ± 0.10 | 0.78 ± 0.08 | 0.74 ± 0.08 | `grade.py::priority_exact` | C0 cannot see the house rubric, so it guesses P2 versus P3. |
| P1 recall (12 tickets) | 0.83 ± 0.09 | 0.95 ± 0.05 | 0.92 ± 0.08 | `grade.py::p1_recall` | Outages are obvious. Security and data loss tickets get missed without the rubric. Each ticket is worth 0.083. |
| Schema validity | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | `grade.py::schema_valid` | Tool-call output follows the schema. |
| Mean input tokens per ticket | 450 ± 100 | 2,300 ± 400 | 2,300 ± 400 | `grade.py::usage_input` | The guide and examples add about 1,850 tokens. |
| Mean output tokens per ticket | 70 ± 25 | 70 ± 25 | 70 ± 25 | `grade.py::usage_output` | The schema fixes the output to 3 short fields. |
| Mean cost per ticket (USD) | 0.0040 ± 0.0012 | 0.0133 ± 0.0035 | 0.0080 ± 0.0021 | `grade.py::cost_usd` | Input tokens drive cost. The numbers assume $5 and $25 per million tokens for Opus and $3 and $15 for Sonnet. |

Expected outcome: no config passes every requirement. C0 should meet R4 and miss R1 and R2. C1 should meet R1 to R3 and miss R4. C2 should come close on both. r01 will measure how much accuracy each cost saving gives up.

I will confirm list prices in the claude-api reference before I save the predictions. If the prices differ from my assumption, I will recompute only the cost row from the token predictions. The yaml will record the prices I used.

## 3. Evaluate

### Build steps (after approval)

1. Save the transcript, `spe/spec/spec.md`, and `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r01 specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. The file starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds the round, the date 2026-10-21, the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, each number with its band and Why, `same_as_last_round: null`, and `naive_guess`. Commit `SPE r01 predict: C1 most accurate, C2 cheapest passing candidate`.
3. Build the agent. The files are `triage/agent.py`, `triage/schema.json`, `triage/prompts/c0.md`, and `triage/prompts/c1.md`. Write the tickets to `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` and the gold labels to `spe/evals/gold/r01-labels.jsonl`. Run the overlap check from D9. Commit `SPE r01 build: triage agent and ticket set`.
4. Write `spe/evals/graders/grade.py`, `spe/evals/graders/selftest.py`, and `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.

### Gates before launch
Each gate must pass before the next step starts. If a gate fails, I fix the problem and run that gate again.

1. **Grader selftest.** The gold file scores 1.00 on every check. An empty output scores 0. A shifted label file scores below 0.20.
2. **Control.** I grade one recorded answer file twice, and both runs must give identical scores (D8).
3. **Dry run.** I run C0 and C2 on 3 tickets each. The outputs must match the schema, token counts must be recorded, and the transcript scan must come back clean.

### Workflow design
- A `ROUND = "r01"` constant holds the round. Prompt text never contains a typed round number.
- There are 9 trial agents, one for each config and chunk of 20 tickets. Each agent runs `python -m triage.agent --config <C> --tickets <chunk>`. Each agent returns rows in this schema: `ticket_id`, `config`, `category`, `priority`, `reason`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `latency_ms`, `error`.
- Trial agents run on Opus.
- Code grades every check. No LLM judge runs in r01 because code can check every label.
- A scan of every trial transcript looks for reads of `spe/evals/gold/`, `spe/evals/graders/`, and `spe/predictions/`. Any trial that peeked is voided and logged.
- Every cell graded wrong gets 2 extra trials. A cell whose trials disagree is marked split. The extra trials are capped at 60 calls.
- A failure analysis agent groups wrong cells into F-numbered types.
- A completeness critic agent checks three things. Every cell has a grade. Every skip is logged. Every predicted number has a measured value.

### Workflow arguments

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROUND` | `"r01"` |
| `configs` | `["C0", "C1", "C2"]` |
| `tickets` | `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` |
| `trials_per_cell` | 1 |
| `extra_trials_cap` | 60 |
| `api_budget_usd` | 5.00 |
| `max_api_calls` | 300 |
| `max_agents` | 12 |

If the next trial would go over a cap, the Workflow skips it and logs the skip.

### Cost estimate (not measured)
The main run makes 180 API calls at about $0.0084 each, which is about $1.50. The extra trials add up to about $0.60. The Workflow agents also use Claude Code tokens. I have not measured that overhead, and I expect it to cost more than the API calls. The $5 cap covers only the API calls made by the triage agent.

## 4. Close-out (after the completion notice)
- Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
- Write `spe/prediction-log.md` with Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Add a "Which Why broke" section under the table. It will say plainly if the naive guess beat my predictions.
- Write `spe/failures.md` with one entry per F-numbered type. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure. The file keeps the original and regraded numbers side by side.
- Add a "Proposed for round r02" table to the spec. Likely candidates are prompt caching on C1 and C2, real tickets, and a cheaper model only if you approve it. Write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- Write `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r01`.

## Rules for this round
- All commits stay local. I will not push. Commit messages will not mention Claude.
- I will never edit `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` after a trial has run.
- I will halt and report if any of these happen: a budget cap is hit, the answer key leaks, the grader breaks, or a decision needs you.
- r01 cannot meet the stop rule. The stop rule needs 3 rounds in a row where predictions match results.
critiques: The plan saves the prompt word for word as the transcript. It turns "correctly" and "cheaply" into requirements R1 to R5. Each requirement has a Test column with a threshold, such as "Category accuracy is at least 0.90" and "Mean cost per ticket is at most $0.006".

The Numbers table gives C0, C1, and C2 a number and a band for every metric. Examples are category accuracy "0.82 ± 0.06 / 0.90 ± 0.05 / 0.87 ± 0.06" and cost "0.0040 / 0.0133 / 0.0080". The table uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Every metric row has a Why column that explains the numbers across configs. For example, the cost row says "Input tokens drive cost" and states the price assumptions. The P1 recall row explains which tickets get missed without the rubric.

The plan names a Workflow harness, spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js. Its "Gates before launch" section requires a grader selftest, a control regrade, and a dry run of C0 and C2 on 3 tickets each before the full run.
The Numbers table has a "Grader check" column. It maps each metric to a named function, such as grade.py::category_exact, grade.py::p1_recall, and grade.py::cost_usd.

The Close-out section writes spe/prediction-log.md with Predicted, Measured, and Verdict columns and a "Which Why broke" section. It seeds round r02 with a "Proposed for round r02" table and spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml.
